title: Illegal dispensary owner charged in rape of 2 girls - NewsBreak
text:
By Dan Alexander ,
4 hours ago
🚨Police said the two assaults happened in August 🚨The suspect was taken into custody outside his Trenton convenience store 🚨He was found with a handgun and 4 lbs of marijuana during his arrest TRENTON — A man who police say ran an illegal marijuana dispensary and convenience store is charged with sexually assaulting two juveniles under the age of 13 in August.
Rasheen Gaither, 51, assaulted one of the girls when she was spending the night at his home, Mercer County Prosecutor Janetta D. Marbrey said. The other assault happened at an illegal dispensary Gaither runs in the city of Trenton.
Charges against owner of illegal dispensary Bagged U Gaither was arrested Friday outside his store, Bagged U, located on Pennington Avenue. During a search of the store police also found four pounds of marijuana and a handgun.
The prosecutor’s office has filed a motion to detain Gaither pending trial.
Gaither is charged with two counts of first-degree aggravated sexual assault, two counts of second-degree sexual assault and one count of second-degree endangering the welfare of a child plus one count of second-degree certain persons not to possess a handgun.
Cough, cough: NJ's favorite lost voice and sore throat remedies Gallery Credit: Dan Zarrow Dan Zarrow, Townsquare Media Water The first thing I reach for when my throat feels even remotely scratchy: A cup of cool water. Gotta keep "the pipes" as lubricated as possible. While caffeinated and carbonated beverages are not a great solution, I have to admit I lean on them often, sick or not. Dan Zarrow, Townsquare Media Salt Water I've heard gargling with salt water can help a sore throat, but I've never had any success. WebMD suggests it can provide short-term relief, and recommends "1/4 to 1/2 teaspoon of salt dissolved in an 8-ounce glass of water water." Traditional Medicinals via Amazon Tea A classic. Unfortunately, I strongly dislike drinking tea. (Hot, iced, or otherwise.) The most popular suggestion I've seen is the Traditional Medicinals "Throat Coat" brand. iStock Honey Supposedly, adding a spoonful of honey makes tea even more effective at allaying a sore throat. And/or more makes it more delicious, I suppose. Mariusz Blach Lemon Again, a potential additive to your soothing hot tea. Or something to suck on by itself, if you're into that sort of thing. Penn Medicine reports "lemons are great for sore throats because they help to break up mucus and provide pain relief." gbh007 Hot Sauce I tried this one by accident last week, by eating an order of boneless buffalo wings. And I have to say, it did provide temporary relief by clearing sinuses and burning away the throat mucus. Unfortunately, despite the power of capsacin, it was not a permanent cure. Dan Zarrow, Townsquare Media Cough Drops I almost always reach for the heavy duty cough drops with benzocaine and menthol to soothe a sore throat. You do have to be careful with some brands of cough drops though — with the amount of sugar in there, they are more like candy than medicine. Getty Stock / ThinkStock Over-the-Counter Medicine Obviously, there is a wide variety of decongestants that will help a head cold to varying degrees. Be sure to follow dosage instructions carefully to avoid overdosing. And be extra careful with taking nighttime medicines, which can cause instant drowsiness and disorientation. Brian Chase Prescription Meds I didn't even realize this was an option for a run-of-the-mill sore throat, until I was at my doctor for a sick visit and strep test a few years ago. He prescribed me a steroid, a one-dose shot of five little pills. And wow, did it work — my voice was back to 100% within hours. This "cure" doesn't work for all cases though. And I did feel pretty loopy afterwards, so I'm not sure I would go this route again unless I was truly desperate. Alexlukin Alcohol Go ahead, take a shot of whiskey. Or a hot toddy, even. It will only provide temporary relief though, as alcohol has a drying effect on your mouth and throat. Of course, if you imbibe enough, you may forget you were sick in the first place. (Be very cognizant and careful about mixing alcohol with medication.) Sebastian Gorczowski Humidifier / Hot Shower The Mayo Clinic suggests either a warm-mist or cool-mist humidifier can ease coughing and congesting, and help to open up your airway. The cool-mist variety is probably best, especially since you won't have to worry about hot-water burn injuries. Keep it clear to prevent mold and mildew from forming, which can cause additional allergy and air quality concerns. adrian825 Rest The only sure-fire "cure" for a sore throats and a lost voice: Vocal rest. Difficult to accomplish sometimes. (Especially when you're reading a weather forecast on the radio every 15 minutes, screaming at your kids, etc.) But it is vitally important to give your vocal cords a rest so they can heal and recuperate. It's important to give your body and mind a rest too — being sick is no fun at all. 2025 9/11 Commemorations in New Jersey (listed alphabetically) Thursday, September 11, 2025 will mark the 24th anniversary of the tragic events in 2001 when planes struck the World Trade Center in Manhattan, the Pentagon in Washington and a field in Pennsylvania. The ceremony includes the Sandpiper Pipes & Drums of Atlantic City performing patriotic songs and a 40 ton patriotic themed sand sculpture by artist John Gowdy. Among the participants: Kevin Shaeffer, Survivor of the 9/11 attack at the Pentagon, Father Michael Duffy, OFM Franciscan brother and homilist of Father Mychal Judge, the New Jersey State Police Honor Guard and the Port Authority Police Department Pipes & Drum Band. Lewis stage at Woodbridge High School starting at 6 p.m. Accused NJ sex predator teachers, school staff this year and last A number of teachers, coaches and school staff around New Jersey have been arrested in 2024 and this year for a range of sexual offenses. Gallery Credit: Erin Vogt (Cape May County Sheriff's Office, Google Maps) Laura Caron Caron, 34, of Cape May Courthouse, was arrested in January 2025 and charged with first-degree aggravated sexual assault and second-degree counts of sexual assault and endangering the welfare of a child. The fifth-grade teacher at Middle Township Elementary School 2 was immediately placed on paid administrative leave, school officials said.
Between 2016 and 2020, the victim and his two siblings lived with Caron when the sexual abuse began, Cape May County Prosecutor Jeffrey Sutherland said.
It was not until December 2024 that police were contacted.
School officials received a tip about a social media post made by the victim’s father, asking about Caron’s now 5-year-old child bearing a resemblance to the victim. (Middlesex County Prosecutor's Office, Google Maps) Axel Palomares Axel Palomares , a teacher at Saint Thomas Aquinas High School, was arrested May 27.
The Spanish teacher and girls' soccer coach was charged with second-degree counts of manufacturing of child sexual abuse material, and endangering the welfare of a child, third-degree possession of child sexual abuse material and fourth-degree invasion of privacy. (linkedin.com julieann-whille, Google Maps) Julie Rizzitello (nee Julie Whille) The 36-year-old Wall Township High School has been accused of having a sexual relationship with a student.
Julie Rizzitello, of Brick, submitted her resignation to the district, days before being arrested on July 3, 2024. Rizzitello engaged in sexual acts with the victim starting earlier this year, according to the Monmouth County Prosecutor's Office.
She was charged with two counts of second-degree sexual assault, third-degree witness tampering and three counts of fourth-degree criminal sexual contact.
(Credit: Linkedin via Justin McGhee) Justin McGhee A Monmouth County teacher and girls basketball coach has been accused of sexually assaulting a student from his high school.
McGhee, of Ocean Township, coached at Middletown High School North, where he led the girls’ basketball team for eight years. The 35-year-old was arrested in January 2025 and charged with second-degree counts of sexual assault and endangering the welfare of a child.
Police said starting in late 2024, McGhee engaged in sexual acts with a victim younger than 18. (Google Maps, Canva, Townsquare Media Illustration) Darrell R Moody Moody, of Plainfield, was arrested in Trenton in August 2024. The former teacher and basketball coach was accused of sexually assaulting a child, repeatedly, over a five year span.
The victim contacted Trenton police in May 2024 to report incidents of sexual assault that began in 2014, when the student was in middle school. Investigators found sexual abuse happened through 2019, when the victim was in high school.
Moody was teaching fifth grade at Parker Elementary School and coaching basketball at Joyce Kilmer Middle School, during that time span.
He was charged with first-degree aggravated sexual assault and second-degree sexual assault, and two counts each of aggravated criminal sexual contact, criminal sexual contact and endangering the welfare of a child. (Monmouth County Prosecutor's Office) Allison Havemann-Niedrach A Monmouth County teacher, then 43, was arrested in late June 2024, similarly accused of a sexual relationship with a student.
Allison Havemann-Niedrach, of Howell, was charged with first-degree aggravated sexual assault and second-degree child endangerment — for alleged activities with a student while she worked at Freehold Intermediate School. She was indicted on charges in March 2025. (Photo credit: Drew University, Google Maps, Morris County Prosecutor's Office) James Wiegand Wiegand , 43, of Sparta, was arrested in March 2025. The Morris County high school teacher and longtime multi-level soccer coach has been accused of sending sexual and suggestive messages to a young teen.
The Parsippany High School social studies teacher was alleged to have sent sexual and suggestive messages via Instagram to the 14-year-old between September and November 2024. He was charged with third-degree endangering the welfare of a child.
In 2024, Wiegand also began his sixth season as assistant coach of the Drew University women's soccer team.
He was suspended from his jobs at both schools, officials confirmed. (Google Maps, Canva, Townsquare Media Illustration) Jessica Sawicki In April 2024, 37-year-old Jessica Sawicki was arrested for alleged activities involving a minor student. The investigation spanned at least three counties — Sawicki was a Point Pleasant resident, working at Hamilton High School West in Mercer County.
She was found meeting a student for alleged sexual activities at Assunpink Wildlife Management Area, according to the Monmouth County Prosecutor's Office.
Sawicki was charged with five counts each of sexual assault and endangering the welfare of a child, all second-degree offenses. She appeared at an April court hearing covered by Asbury Park Press.
(Google Maps) Ryan Ramsay In February 2025, the longtime Ocean County high school teacher and basketball coach was charged with sexual assault from incidents that happened 13 years ago.
Ramsay, the head boys coach and social studies teacher at Manchester Township High School, was charged with sexual assault by someone with supervisory authority over a minor.
The victim was a then-17-year-old senior, who did not report the incidents until 2025. Officials said to New Jersey 101.5 that Ramsay stopped coaching the team in January and was no longer teaching. (Bergen County Sheriff's Office) Amy Dovidio A 46-year-old married art teacher was accused of sexually assaulting a teen student multiple times in several locations, including at Garfield Middle School, according to Bergen County Prosecutor Mark Musella.
Amy Dovidio , of Pompton Plains, was arrested in February 2024 on charges that included aggravated sexual assault, endangering the welfare of a child and criminal sexual contact.
(CarteretMiddleSchool.org, Google Maps) Jeffrey Munguia Also in April 2024, a 32-year-old former middle school teacher in Middlesex County was charged with the sexual assault of a former student. Jeffrey Munguia had been a staff member at Carteret Middle School, teaching English Language Arts, or ELA.
Munguia, a North Bergen resident, was charged with second-degree counts of sexual assault and endangering the welfare of a child.
He was no longer a teacher in the district at the time of his arrest, according to the prosecutor's office. (Google Maps) Jack Wilder Wilder, 26, of Somerville and formerly of Hoboken, was charged with one count of possession of child pornography and two counts of enticement of a minor.
Federal prosecutors said that in February 2024, the then-history teacher at a charter school in Plainfield, contacted a minor on a mobile payment app and offered to pay the victim for sexual acts. The minor victim also sent Wilder sexually explicit photos, police said.
Wilder was initially questioned in July 2024, after arriving in New York from a trip to Iceland. Law enforcement searched his cell phone and found child sexual abuse material.
(Monmouth County Prosecutor's Office) Thomas R. Carraher A 26-year-old teacher and sports coach in Monmouth County was accused of offering to pay cash for a sex act and sending sexually explicit media of himself to a person he thought was a 14-year-old girl, the Monmouth County Prosecutor's Office announced in January 2024.
Thomas R. Carraher, of Howell, was charged with attempted endangering the welfare of a child, attempted promotion of obscene material to a minor, and attempted criminal sexual contact.
Carraher was a teacher at Mahala F. Atchison Elementary School in Tinton Falls, as well as a girls basketball coach at Shrewsbury Borough School. He was suspended from both jobs, pending the investigation. (Bergen County Sheriff's Office) Kurt Zimmermann In February 2024, a married teacher from Rockaway was accused of sexually molesting a student over a decade ago.
Kurt Zimmermann w as arrested in Paramus and charged with three counts of third-degree aggravated criminal sexual contact and second-degree endangering the welfare of a child.
The sexual conduct recently reported to police took place in 2013 at Westwood Regional Middle School and at Westwood Regional High School, according to the Bergen County Prosecutor's Office. (Bergen County Sheriff's Office) Phillip Porter A 76-year-old Hackensack public school custodian was accused of sexually assaulting a 9-year-old girl.
Phillip Porter , of Hackensack, was arrested in March 2024 and charged with aggravated sexual assault, sexual assault by contact and endangering the welfare of a child.
Hackensack police had contacted the Bergen County Prosecutor’s Office Special Victims Unit regarding sexual assault of a juvenile that happened "in the past." (HCPO, Google Maps) Omer Sogutcu Sogutcu, of Garfield was arrested in June 2025, accused of exposing his genitals to two students and asking for sexual acts.
The alleged offenses happened in October 2024 at Hudson Arts and Science Middle School, where Sogutcu was an IT professional.
The computer support staffer at aThe alleged offenses happened in October at Hudson Arts and Science Middle School, where Sogutcu is as an IT professional, Hudson County Prosecutor Esther Suarez said.
He was charged with two counts each of second-degree sexual assault by contact and third-degree endangering the welfare of a child. (Google maps, Canva Townsquare Media Illustration Steven Gordon [no photo available] A 67-year-old high school teacher in North Jersey was accused of making criminal sexual contact with a student in May 2024.
Steven Gordon, of Jersey City, faced fourth-degree criminal sexual contact and second-degree endangering the welfare of a child, Hudson County Prosecutor Esther Suarez said.
In February 2025, Gordon pleaded guilty to a lesser charge.
